players.product: power management passive components (resistors, capacitors) for Rubin boards

quarterly_data.signal: Vishay's 10-K lists its capacity expansion projects: expansion of the Newport wafer fab (acquired from Nexperia in 2024, to be used to further develop and scale SiC MOSFETs and diodes, and expected to start generating profit in 2026), a 12-inch wafer fab in Itzehoe, Germany adjacent to its existing 8-inch fab, a new site in Mexico for power inductors and non-linear resistors, a resistor manufacturing expansion in Mexico, and expanded diode manufacturing in Taiwan and Turin, Italy. It is also outsourcing production of some commodity products to subcontractors to create incremental capacity for higher-growth products.
quarterly_data.figure: 12-inch Itzehoe fab; Newport SiC MOSFET/diode fab; Mexico inductor/resistor sites; diode expansion in Taiwan and Turin

quarterly_data.signal: Vishay invested $273 million in capital expenditures in 2025, 82% of it in capacity expansion projects for high growth product lines including its wafer fab expansions, and planned for at least 70% of 2026 capital expenditures to go to such capacity expansion projects. The contractual obligations table (payments due by period; unit not printed in the saved text) includes estimated costs to complete the MOSFETs wafer fab of 238,800 (226,400 in 2026) and purchase commitments of 89,145, which represent estimated minimum commitments under long-term arrangements with subcontractors, suppliers and other business partners to ensure access to external capacity and supplies.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex $273 million (82% capacity expansion); at least 70% of 2026 capex for capacity expansion; MOSFETs wafer fab cost to complete 238,800 (226,400 in 2026); minimum purchase commitments 89,145 (unit not printed)

quarterly_data.signal: End-of-period backlog (dollars in thousands) was $1,314,100 in the fourth quarter of 2025 versus $1,051,500 in the fourth quarter of 2024, with a fourth-quarter 2025 book-to-bill ratio of 1.20 (0.97 in the third quarter of 2025); the 10-K states book-to-bill and backlog increased significantly versus the prior fiscal quarter and the fourth fiscal quarter of 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 2025 backlog $1,314,100 thousand (Q4 2024: $1,051,500 thousand); Q4 2025 book-to-bill 1.20
